newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money market rates stable.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money market rates stable.

text.p: Croatian money market rates were steady on Thursday in slow trade, as banks' liquidity came under pressure ahead of pension payments.
"The banks' accounts are depleting, so demand is high," a trader said.
Commercial banks' accounts totalled 410 million kuna on Wednesday, or 76 million less than the previous day.
Fresh money market loans were put at 17.8 million kuna at 0900 GMT, while 10 million was left unmatched on the demand side.
Most new borrowings were call money granted at a steady 8.0 percent. Two week funds were granted at a stable 11 percent, and two-month money at 16 percent.
Commercial banks had 7.5 million kuna in outstanding lombard loans, down from Wednesday's 9.25.

Overnight trade totalled 15 million kuna, as one bank borrowed two million to square its position and the rest was used to mantain banks' mandatory reserves. -- Davor Huic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
